d: THE LIBRARY, SIGNED OUT, 2026-10-31, AI MODE: 'The Marxists Internet Archive (MIA), located at marxists.org, is a non-profit, volunteer-run digital library that hosts a vast multilingual collection of communist, socialist, anarchist, and left-wing texts.' Fact table (founded 1990, 'Zodiac'; over 180,000 documents across 80+ languages); core collections; MIA Publications; copyright controversies (the 2014 MECW takedown).
reading: The innocent reading first. Asked for the library, AI Mode describes it, its collections and scope, its print arm and its licensing, and the takedown of 2014.
findings: THE LIBRARY AT ITS GRAIN. Author archives, subject sections, volunteer translation and the public-domain basis are carried; the 2014 removal of the English Collected Works at Lawrence & Wishart's order is given ('The 2014 MECW Takedown').

THE COUNT AND THE DATE. 'Over 180,000 documents across 80+ languages' and 'Founded 1990 (Originally by a user known as "Zodiac")'. The MIA's introduction (last updated 21 April 2026) gives 'over 400,000 documents and 1.1 TB of data (April 2026)' in 83 languages, and dates its present form to 1998, with an earlier history on a page not read here.

THE CHARTER NOT CARRIED. The MIA's sixth tenet, 'We do not ‘judge’ writers', and its 2007 end of 'dividing all writers into Marxists and non-Marxists' are absent. #1725 reads that as the holder condition: a writer stays in the record whatever verdict a party passed on them.
analysis: The library composed accurately at the level of its sections, with a count from an earlier state of the site. What it leaves out is the terms on which it holds: its charter's refusal to judge writers, which is what keeps the losing side of every split on its shelves.

atoms.reference: A seven-tenet Charter (free, non-profit, democratic, full disclosure, politically independent, does not 'judge' writers, archival priority); the 2007 end of the Marxist/non-Marxist division; public domain unless noted.

evidence.record_quote: MIA abides by seven fundamental tenets found in our Charter : (1) We will always be 100% Free; (2) We will always be a non-profit organization; (3) We will always be based on democratic decision making; (4) We will always have full disclosure; (5) We will always remain politically independent; (6) We do not ‘judge’ writers; (7) Our priority is to provide archival information.
In 2007, we terminated our former practice of dividing all writers into Marxists and non-Marxists , and instead offer an index of Selected Marxist Writers in most language sections.
All material within these Archives, unless noted otherwise, is public domain . MIA-created material is protected by the Creative Commons License .
